risks.basis: THIS FILE has a confirmed defect on record
risks.risk: api/sd-data.js authorised law_clients, law_matters and law_deadlines on the LICENCE KEY ALONE -- no employee session at all. A licence key is shipped to the browser and readable by anyone who can open the app, so the effective authorisation was 'opened the app'. law_matters names the client and the matter; law_clients is the client list. MEASURED BEFORE THE FIX rather than inferred: all SIX pairs (three resources by read and write) answered 200 with no token, against a control where law_invoices/read answered 401 -- so 'open' was established against a gated sibling rather than assumed. THIS WAS A KNOWN, DOCUMENTED RESIDUAL, NOT A DISCOVERY, and that is the honest framing: the rollout comment beside the LAW_RESOURCES table named these three as deliberately deferred because Vercel ships the page and the endpoint together, so flipping them mid-day would fail a staff member with the app already open. The fifteen extended resources were the canary and the written trigger was 'quiet for a full working day'. What made it actionable now is that the canary has been quiet six days AND the client half was confirmed rather than assumed -- sairnlaw.html:1509 sdnData() sets X-SD-Auth on every data call whenever a token exists, not conditionally per resource. FIXED with the same mechanism law_trusttx was flipped with on 2026-09-16: three entries in SD_SESSION_GATED plus three in SD_GATE_APP, six lines. All six pairs now answer 403 FORBIDDEN. A SESSION gate and not a ROLE gate, deliberately -- owner, attorney and paralegal all legitimately work clients, matters and deadlines and all three are driven green. DISCLOSED RATHER THAN TIDIED: the endpoint now answers two codes for one condition, 401 NO_SESSION from the inline gate for the fifteen and 403 FORBIDDEN from the shared gate for these four, widening a pre-existing split from one resource to four; unifying is a client-visible contract change and is recorded rather than decided.

risks.basis: THIS FILE has a confirmed defect on record
risks.risk: All twelve SAIRNscape resources in api/sd-data.js dispatched on the licence hash alone with NO session check of any kind, and the licence key is shipped to the browser and readable by anyone who can open sairnscape.html -- so the key WAS the authorisation. Two of the twelve are Tier A on integrity: `invoices` (SAIRNscape's money row; its write branch already refuses a non-numeric amount because a string one reached a fold and printed -99450 on a tax report) and `scp_quotes` (the priced quote every invoice descends from). Identical shape to law_trusttx (gated 2026-09-16), SF_RESOURCES and SDN_RESOURCES; SAIRNscape was swept with none of the three. Fixed by adding both to SD_SESSION_GATED for read AND write with SD_GATE_APP entries pinning each to 'sairnscape' -- 403 FORBIDDEN without a session, plus the shared active-credential re-check, so a deactivated employee is refused on a token that still verifies. THE NAME IS THE PART THAT MAKES THIS FIX FAILABLE IN SILENCE: SAIRNscape claimed the bare name `invoices` before the scp_ convention existed, so the storage table is scp_invoices and the RESOURCE the dispatch tests for is `invoices`. A gate written against the table name gates nothing at all and every refusal arm anywhere still passes -- the new suite carries an arm whose only job is that distinction. NO CLIENT CHANGE WAS NEEDED AND THAT WAS MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED, which is the half that has broken apps three times here: scpData() attaches X-SD-Auth on every call whenever a token exists (sairnscape.html:2107) with no per-call withSession flag to forget -- the thing that had to be repaired in sairndesign.html, where 18 of 19 call sites never passed it -- every call site for both resources goes through that one helper, and both login paths store the token before scpApplyLoggedIn -> scpInit -> scpSyncFromServer. Arms assert all three against the shipped page rather than against the commit message. DRIVEN TO FAIL BEFORE IT WAS BELIEVED: removing the SD_SESSION_GATED entries takes the new suite to 9/18, removing the SD_GATE_APP pins to 11/18, and renaming the entry to the storage-table name to 16/18. LIVE-VERIFIED against https://sairn.vercel.app/api/sd-data by tools/scp_session_gate_live_probe.py: both resources, both verbs, 403 FORBIDDEN on a licence key alone, against a control (scp_vendors) still answering 200 so the result is a split and not a lockout, plus the DEPLOYED page read back for the X-SD-Auth header. The probe is adapted from the SAIRNlegacy one and the adaptation is the part worth noting: SAIRNlegacy's bespoke gate answers 401 NO_SESSION while this shared one answers 403 FORBIDDEN, so a byte-copy would have reported a working gate as FAILED -- bug class 22.

risks.basis: THIS FILE has a confirmed defect on record
risks.risk: SAIRNscape's 'customers' resource dispatched on the licence hash alone, with no session check of any kind, for READ and WRITE -- and the row carries a customer's NAME, PHONE, EMAIL and STREET ADDRESS. The licence key is shipped to the browser and readable by anyone who can open sairnscape.html, so it was the whole authorisation. PROVEN LIVE WITH A CONTROL before the fix: on SCP-DEMO-2026 with no session token, read customers answered 200 and returned a row with all four fields, and write customers with an id-less payload answered 400 from the handler body -- so the gate did not fire, and nothing was stored because api/sd-data.js:4769 refuses before any store call. The controls are what make it a finding rather than a guess: invoices and scp_quotes on the SAME bare key answered 403 both, so the gate existed, worked, and did not cover this one. THE ROOT CAUSE IS NOT THE GATE, IT IS A CORRECTION THAT STOPPED AT THE PROSE. The 2026-10-05 sweep that armed SAIRNscape scoped itself to Tier A and was right to; 'customers' is carried B/B in docs/CRITICALITY-TIERS.md while its own confidentiality cell had already been corrected to read 'A CUSTOMER's NAME, PHONE, EMAIL AND STREET ADDRESS'. The basis was fixed and the LETTER was not, and the letter is what the sweep reads, so the resource was invisible to the mechanism that would have gated it. Fixed by adding the resource to SD_SESSION_GATED and SD_GATE_APP in one edit; the B->A retier that would have prevented it is owed and is held by another session. The client needed no change and that was checked rather than assumed: customers is read only inside scpSyncFromServer()'s resource loop at sairnscape.html:2734, reached only after login, and the two already-gated resources sit in the same loop.

risks.risk: sairnscape.html scpData: the no-licence guard at :2077 returned null WITHOUT touching scpLastErr, so after any real 4xx on the same resource a later call with no licence INHERITED that status and scpWriteRefused() answered true for a call the server never saw. scpSendDesignToQuote branches on exactly that predicate, so the row was NOT QUEUED -- the whole retry path skipped -- the toast quoted an unrelated earlier row's reason as a server judgement, and a row already in the queue was marked 'refused' and never retried again. risks.risk: sairnscape.html's pricing section heading read 'Simple. Honest. No per-user games.' over 'Flat monthly fee. Unlimited users. Cancel anytime.' -- a blanket claim about the pricing model -- while the Starter card thirteen lines below it reads 'Up to 3 users'. Professional and Business genuinely are unlimited; Starter is not, and Starter is the card a first-time reader prices against, so the claim has already influenced the decision by the time the contradiction arrives. Same class as the 'QuickBooks integration' line removed from this same file on 2026-09-02: a purchase-influencing claim the product withdraws. Fixed by saying what is true -- flat fee, never billed per user, unlimited users on Professional and Business, Starter covers 3 -- rather than by deleting the sentence, because the fee really is flat and there really is no per-seat billing.
